intervals.label: construction begins
intervals.locator: JLab news story "Fifteen Years of Beam on Target", section "Great Expectations"
intervals.note: Jefferson Lab gives the month (February 1987) for the start of construction; no official page consulted states a day.
intervals.quote: Construction on what came to be called the Continuous Electron Beam Accelerator Facility began in February of 1987

intervals.label: first beam delivered to an experimental hall
intervals.locator: JLab news story "Fifteen Years of Beam on Target", opening paragraph
intervals.quote: On July 1, 1994, Jefferson Lab's accelerator delivered an electron beam into one of its experimental halls for the first time.

intervals.label: 4 GeV era (design energy reached 1995)
intervals.locator: Freyberger et al., IPAC2015 MOXGB2, section Introduction
intervals.note: Year precision. Re-sourced (2026-10-26) from a JLab accelerator paper; the earlier record rested on an encyclopaedia entry. The 4 GeV design energy is the machine's original specification (the paper: "three times the original design energy of 4 GeV"); LINAC2012 TH3A02 (Pilat) says "started operations in 1995" and "Designed for a maximum energy of 6 GeV", a different statement of the design figure. The era ends when 6 GeV was reached (2000).
intervals.quote: The CEBAF design included 42 cryomodules with each cryomodule containing 8 SRF cavities to achieve the design energy of 4 GeV. CEBAF reached design energy in 1995.

beam_energy.locator: Freyberger et al., IPAC2015 MOXGB2, section Introduction
beam_energy.note: Original design energy, reached in 1995 (re-sourced from the JLab paper).
beam_energy.quote: The CEBAF design included 42 cryomodules with each cryomodule containing 8 SRF cavities to achieve the design energy of 4 GeV. CEBAF reached design energy in 1995.

intervals.label: 6 GeV era (until the 12 GeV Upgrade shutdown)
intervals.locator: Freyberger et al., IPAC2015 MOXGB2, Introduction; CERN Courier, 23 July 2014; Pilat, LINAC2012 TH3A02
intervals.note: Start year-precision (2000) and end May 2012: "In May 2012, the accelerator was shut down for its 12 GeV upgrade." (CERN Courier); Pilat: "its last run at 6 GeV successfully completed in the spring 2012". The earlier record dated the start to 6 August 2000 from an encyclopaedia entry; no JLab or paper source read gives the day, so the year is recorded.
intervals.quote: The energy reach of 6 GeV of CEBAF was establish in 2000; CEBAF operated at energies up to 6 GeV until 2012.

beam_energy.locator: Freyberger et al., IPAC2015 MOXGB2, Introduction
beam_energy.note: Maximum energy of the 6 GeV era ("enhanced design energy"), re-sourced from the JLab paper.
beam_energy.quote: The energy reach of 6 GeV of CEBAF was establish in 2000; CEBAF operated at energies up to 6 GeV until 2012.

intervals.label: 12 GeV Upgrade: 6 GeV operations ended, installation
intervals.locator: CERN Courier, 23 July 2014; Freyberger et al., IPAC2015 MOXGB2, section The 12GeV Upgrade
intervals.note: Construction started in 2009 and overlapped with 6 GeV operations ("This design was completed and construction started in 2009, construction overlapped with 6 GeV beam operations for work that did not impact CEBAF operations."). The end is the start of beam commissioning: "the accelerator tunnel portion of the upgrade was sufficiently complete by the end of 2013 to start of beam commissioning activities" (same paper), December 2013 for the first beam back ("bringing the accelerator back online last December", CERN Courier, July 2014).
intervals.quote: In May 2012, the accelerator was shut down for its 12 GeV upgrade.

intervals.label: 12 GeV Upgrade: beam commissioning (first beams to Hall D, 7 May 2014)
intervals.locator: Freyberger et al., IPAC2015 MOXGB2, section The 12GeV Upgrade; CERN Courier, 23 July 2014; review arXiv:2408.16880, Introduction
intervals.note: Milestones in the CERN Courier report of July 2014: full upgrade-energy acceleration of 2.2 GeV in one pass by 5 February; three-pass 6.11 GeV beams on 1 April ("the first data of the 12-GeV era"); on 7 May the energy was raised to 10.5 GeV through all 5.5 passes and 10.5 GeV beam went into the new Hall D ("The operators continued to push the upgraded machine, and early on 7 May the energy was increased to 10.5 GeV through the entire 5.5 passes. In the last minutes of the day, 10.5 GeV beam was delivered into the new Hall D complex."). IPAC 2015: "The program for Fall 2015 and beyond is to operate CEBAF at the design energy of 12 GeV." The end is the start of the experiments at the higher energy (next interval). A JLab news item reports 12.065 GeV electrons delivered to Hall D on "Dec. 14" in the commissioning of the upgrade; the page prints no year, so it is not used for a date.
intervals.quote: 6 GeV beam operations terminated in 2012, and the accelerator tunnel portion of the upgrade was sufficiently complete by the end of 2013 to start of beam commissioning activities.

intervals.label: 12 GeV era (higher-energy experiments)
intervals.note: Year precision: the review dates the experiments at the higher beam energy to "Since 2016"; the review also writes of "the onset of CEBAF 12 GeV era operation" in 2014 and the CERN Courier recorded the first data of the 12-GeV era in April 2014 (a 6.11 GeV beam), so the start is not a sharp date. The headline 12 GeV is the maximum design energy: the review reports "The final energy to Hall D was lowered from 12.0 to 11.6 GeV to mitigate overall fault rates."
intervals.quote: The major construction of the accelerator upgrade to 12 GeV was completed in a six-month shut-down at the end of 2011 and a long shut-down throughout 2013. Since 2016, nuclear physics experiments at the higher beam energy have been performed.

beam_energy.display: 12 GeV (maximum; 11.6 GeV to Hall D in operation)
beam_energy.note: The maximum design energy of the upgraded machine; the final energy to Hall D was later lowered from 12.0 to 11.6 GeV to reduce fault rates (the review, section IV).
beam_energy.quote: This superconducting linac has achieved 12 GeV beam energy by adding 11 new high-performance cryomodules containing eighty-eight superconducting cavities that have operated CW at an average accelerating gradient of 20 MV/m.

intervals.label: 12 GeV Upgrade dedication
intervals.locator: JLab Archives page, closing paragraph of the history summary
intervals.note: This is the dedication ceremony; earlier operation is recorded in the first-beam (1994), 4 GeV (1995) and 6 GeV (2000) intervals.
intervals.quote: On Wednesday, May 2, 2018, the CEBAF 12 GeV Upgrade Dedication Ceremony took place

name: Continuous Electron Beam Accelerator Facility
notes: kind is recorded as `linac`; CEBAF is technically a recirculating (racetrack) superconducting linac, which ACCELERATOR_KINDS does not have a dedicated value for.

Eras (2026-10-26, follow-ups 2): the 4 GeV (1995), 6 GeV (2000 to May 2012) and 12 GeV (from 2016) eras are sourced to JLab accelerator papers and the CERN Courier; the 12 GeV Upgrade has its own dated intervals (shutdown and installation May 2012 to December 2013, beam commissioning from December 2013). The 1987 construction start, the 1994 first beam and the 2018 dedication still rest on an encyclopaedia entry (src:jlab-wikipedia) and are unchanged.

beam_energy.note: Maximum design energy after the 12 GeV Upgrade (the 12 GeV era interval carries the dated value; the Hall D operating energy was lowered to 11.6 GeV). Original design energy was 4 GeV, 6 GeV from 2000 to 2012.
beam_energy.quote: The CEBAF energy was recently upgraded from 6 GeV to 12 GeV, and an additional experimental area was added to support the highest-energy experiments.

summary.plain: Jefferson Lab's main particle accelerator, which fires a continuous beam of electrons at nuclear targets in four experimental halls. It reached its 4 GeV design energy in 1995, was raised to 6 GeV in 2000, and was upgraded to 12 GeV between 2012 and 2016.
summary.technical: Continuous Electron Beam Accelerator Facility: a superconducting recirculating (racetrack) electron linac at Jefferson Lab; first beam 1994-07-01, design energy of 4 GeV reached in 1995, 6 GeV from 2000 to May 2012, then the 12 GeV Upgrade (shutdown May 2012, beam commissioning from December 2013, first beams to the new Hall D on 7 May 2014, higher-energy experiments since 2016).
